main_body: Stilted hut: a large plank roof (rows 0-21) over a plank wall with a small door and window (rows 22-36), a platform edge, and thin stilts
top_band: Roof slope in mid-brown planks, rows 2-18, with a light cap line at rows 0-2 and a darker eave band at rows 16-21; no distinct lighter top band
evidence: The roof is a large foreshortened slope that spans most of the upper part of the object. It has a dark eave at rows 18-21 that shades the wall below. Under it sits a separate vertical wall face with an inset dark door frame and window. The platform edge at rows 35-37 is a light band that overhangs the stilts. The roof is the same tone as the wall and reads partly like a plank wall, and there is no crisp front-edge line. The roof-over-wall structure is still clear, so I pass it narrowly.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tone, which is acceptable. The wood ramp has only about 4 steps (light orange, mid, dark brown, deep brown). The roof and wall are vertical plank stripes with large flat single-colour areas, roughly 4x10 px each. There are no tile scallops, grain dots, or per-plank highlights beyond the stripes. The stilts and platform are thin and simple. Each tile carries only a few colours, far below the references' tile-rich roof tiles, timber framing, and stone speckle.
